mergedParams.userDescription: Smooth slide-in positioning. internal effects for text, video, images

output.title: Smooth Slide-in with Internal Effects for Media

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset module called 'smoothSlideIn' that provides elegant slide-in positioning animations for text, video, and image elements. This effect should use generic AnimationRange animations to smoothly translate elements from off-screen positions into their final locations with customizable direction, distance, and easing. The effect should accept parameters for slideDirection ('left', 'right', 'top', 'bottom', 'topLeft', 'topRight', 'bottomLeft', 'bottomRight'), slideDistance (in pixels or viewport units), duration (milliseconds), delay (milliseconds), and easingType ('ease-out', 'ease-in-out', 'spring'). The animation should use GPU-accelerated transform3d for optimal performance, starting with the element completely off-screen and ending at translate3d(0,0,0). Include a subtle opacity fade from 0.3 to 1 during the first 40% of the animation for a softer entrance. The effect should return a single generic effect object with provider mode and targetIds, using AnimationRange keyframes that smoothly interpolate the translateX/Y and opacity values.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (AnimationRange[]). AnimationRange structure: For horizontal slides use translateX with prog [0, 0.6, 1] and values like [-slideDistance, -slideDistance*0.1, 0], for vertical use translateY, for diagonal combine both. Include opacity range with prog [0, 0.4, 1] and val [0.3, 0.95, 1]. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: delay || 0, duration: duration || 800, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges: [translateX/Y ranges, opacity range], easingType }. Input schema: z.object({ slideDirection: z.enum(['left', 'right', 'top', 'bottom', 'topLeft', 'topRight', 'bottomLeft', 'bottomRight']), slideDistance: z.number().default(100), duration: z.number().default(800), delay: z.number().optional(), easingType: z.enum(['ease-out', 'ease-in-out', 'spring']).default('ease-out'), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal waveform effect preset called 'audioReactiveSlide' that creates audio-synchronized sliding movements for media elements. This effect should react to bass frequencies in the audio, creating subtle horizontal or vertical sliding movements that pulse with the beat. The effect should use waveform type 'translate' with customizable axis ('x' or 'y'), reacting primarily to bass frequencies (20-250Hz) with adjustable sensitivity (0.1 to 1.0) and threshold (0.3 to 0.8). Include parameters for baseOffset (the neutral position), maxSlide (maximum slide distance in pixels), returnSpeed (how quickly it returns to neutral), and smoothing (interpolation factor). The effect should create a 'breathing' slide motion where elements shift position based on bass intensity, with smooth transitions back to the base position. Add an optional 'inverse' mode that slides in the opposite direction. The waveform effect should use provider mode targeting specific element IDs.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: waveform (audio-reactive). Waveform configuration: { type: 'translate', axis: params.axis || 'x', audioProperty: 'bass', sensitivity: params.sensitivity || 0.5, threshold: params.threshold || 0.4, baseValue: params.baseOffset || 0, amplitude: params.maxSlide || 30, returnSpeed: params.returnSpeed || 0.2, smoothing: params.smoothing || 0.3, inverse: params.inverse || false }. Effect data: { type: 'waveform', start: 0, duration: 'parent', mode: 'provider', targetIds, props: waveformConfig }. Input schema: z.object({ axis: z.enum(['x', 'y']).default('x'), baseOffset: z.number().default(0), maxSlide: z.number().default(30), sensitivity: z.number().min(0.1).max(1).default(0.5), threshold: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.4), returnSpeed: z.number().min(0.1).max(1).default(0.2), smoothing: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.3), inverse: z.boolean().optional(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Build a sophisticated internal effect preset called 'cascadeSlideIn' that creates a staggered slide-in effect for multiple elements, perfect for text lines, image galleries, or video grids. This effect should combine multiple generic effects with calculated delays to create a cascading animation where each element slides in sequentially. Accept parameters for slideFrom ('left', 'right', 'alternate'), cascadeDelay (milliseconds between each element), itemDuration (duration per element), overlapFactor (0-1, how much animations overlap), and easingCurve. Each element should slide from 120% off-screen to its final position, with a scale transformation from 0.85 to 1, and opacity from 0 to 1. The effect should calculate individual delays based on element index, creating a smooth wave-like entrance. Include an optional 'reverse' parameter to cascade from last to first element. Support both linear and exponential delay patterns.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: combined (multiple generic effects). AnimationRange structure per element: translateX with prog [0, 0.3, 0.7, 1] and values based on slideFrom direction, scale with prog [0, 0.5, 1] and val [0.85, 0.95, 1], opacity with prog [0, 0.3, 1] and val [0, 0.8, 1]. Effect data per element: { type: 'generic', start: calculatedDelay, duration: itemDuration, mode: 'provider', targetIds: [elementId], ranges: [translateX, scale, opacity], easingType }. Delay calculation: baseDelay + (index * cascadeDelay * (1 - overlapFactor)). Input schema: z.object({ slideFrom: z.enum(['left', 'right', 'alternate']).default('left'), cascadeDelay: z.number().default(100), itemDuration: z.number().default(600), overlapFactor: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.3), easingCurve: z.enum(['ease-out', 'ease-in-out', 'spring']).default('ease-out'), reverse: z.boolean().optional(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [...effectArray] }

prompts.prompt: Develop an internal effect preset called 'elasticSlideIn' that uses spring physics simulation for natural, bouncy slide-in animations. This effect should simulate elastic motion with overshoot and settling, creating a playful entrance for UI elements. The effect uses generic AnimationRange but with custom spring easing calculations to create realistic physics. Accept parameters for springTension (50-200), springDamping (5-20), initialVelocity (-100 to 100), slideAngle (0-360 degrees for any direction), and overshootAmount (1.0-1.3). The animation should calculate spring physics keyframes with at least 8 progression points, including the overshoot past the target position and the settling oscillation. Add subtle rotation (-5 to 5 degrees) that correlates with the slide velocity for added dynamism. Include an optional 'trail' effect that adds a motion blur filter during rapid movement phases.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic with physics simulation. AnimationRange calculation: Generate 8-12 keyframes using spring physics formula. For position: prog [0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.6, 0.75, 0.85, 1], values calculated from spring equation with overshoot. Rotation: prog [0, 0.3, 0.6, 1] with val [0, maxRotation, -maxRotation*0.3, 0]. Optional blur: prog [0, 0.2, 0.8, 1] with val [0, blurAmount, blurAmount*0.5, 0]. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: calculatedSpringDuration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges: [translateX, translateY, rotate, blur?], easingType: 'linear' }. Spring calculation: Use damped harmonic oscillator equation. Input schema: z.object({ springTension: z.number().min(50).max(200).default(100), springDamping: z.number().min(5).max(20).default(10), initialVelocity: z.number().min(-100).max(100).default(0), slideAngle: z.number().min(0).max(360).default(0), overshootAmount: z.number().min(1).max(1.3).default(1.15), includeTrail: z.boolean().optional(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'magneticSlideIn' that simulates magnetic attraction, where elements accelerate as they get closer to their final position. This effect should create a unique slide-in where the animation starts very slowly, then rapidly accelerates in the middle, creating a 'snapping' feel as if magnetically pulled into place. Accept parameters for magnetStrength (0.1-1.0), pullDistance (initial distance from target), pullDirection (angle in degrees), resistanceZone (0-0.5, portion of animation with resistance), and snapSpeed (final acceleration multiplier). The effect should use custom easing curves that simulate magnetic field strength decreasing with distance. Include a subtle scale 'squash' effect (0.95-1.05) at the moment of 'contact' to enhance the physical feel. Add optional particle effects (via CSS shadows) that trail behind the element during acceleration.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic with magnetic physics. AnimationRange structure: Custom magnetic easing with prog [0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 0.95, 1], translateX/Y values calculated using inverse square law for magnetic attraction. Scale 'squash': prog [0, 0.7, 0.85, 0.92, 1] with val [1, 1, 0.95, 1.05, 1]. Optional shadow trail: multiple box-shadows with decreasing opacity. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges: [translateX, translateY, scale, boxShadow?], easingType: 'linear' }. Magnetic calculation: acceleration = magnetStrength / (distance^2). Input schema: z.object({ magnetStrength: z.number().min(0.1).max(1).default(0.5), pullDistance: z.number().default(200), pullDirection: z.number().min(0).max(360).default(180), resistanceZone: z.number().min(0).max(0.5).default(0.2), snapSpeed: z.number().min(1).max(3).default(1.5), includeTrail: z.boolean().optional(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset called 'liquidSlideIn' that creates a fluid, liquid-like slide animation with morphing and distortion effects. This effect simulates liquid motion using a combination of transforms and SVG filters for realistic fluid dynamics. Accept parameters for viscosity (0.1-1.0, affects flow speed), surfaceTension (affects wobble), flowDirection, turbulence (adds random perturbations), and dropletMode (splits into multiple streams). The animation should use skewX/Y transforms that change based on velocity, creating a stretching effect during movement. Add a custom SVG turbulence filter that creates rippling distortions, strongest during acceleration phases. Include bezier curve path animation for non-linear sliding trajectories. The effect should feel organic and fluid, as if the element is made of liquid sliding into place.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic with SVG filters. AnimationRange structure: translateX/Y with bezier curve interpolation, skewX with prog [0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1] and val [0, 15*direction, 0, -5*direction, 0], skewY similar pattern. SVG filter: feTurbulence with animated baseFrequency, feDisplacementMap for distortion. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges: [translateX, translateY, skewX, skewY, filter], easingType: 'cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55)', svgFilter: turbulenceFilterDef }. Bezier path: Calculate control points based on flowDirection and turbulence. Input schema: z.object({ viscosity: z.number().min(0.1).max(1).default(0.5), surfaceTension: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.3), flowDirection: z.enum(['linear', 'arc', 'wave', 'spiral']).default('arc'), turbulence: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.2), dropletMode: z.boolean().optional(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Build an internal waveform effect preset called 'rhythmicSlidePosition' that creates complex, multi-layered audio-reactive sliding movements. This effect should combine multiple waveform effects responding to different frequency bands, creating rich, musical positioning animations. The effect responds to bass for primary movement, mids for secondary oscillation, and treble for micro-vibrations. Accept parameters for primaryAxis ('x' or 'y'), secondaryAxis (perpendicular), bassResponse (base movement amplitude), midResponse (oscillation amplitude), trebleResponse (vibration amplitude), phaseOffset (creates spiral/circular motion), and smoothingFactor. Each frequency band should have different sensitivity and threshold settings. The combined motion creates organic, dance-like sliding that perfectly synchronizes with music. Include an optional 'echo' mode that creates trailing ghost positions.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: combined waveform effects. Waveform configurations: 1) Bass translate on primaryAxis with sensitivity 0.6, threshold 0.3, amplitude bassResponse. 2) Mid translate on secondaryAxis with sensitivity 0.4, threshold 0.5, amplitude midResponse, phase shifted. 3) Treble translate with micro amplitude on both axes. Optional echo: Additional effects with decreasing amplitude and increasing delay. Effect data array: [{ type: 'waveform', props: bassConfig }, { type: 'waveform', props: midConfig }, { type: 'waveform', props: trebleConfig }]. Input schema: z.object({ primaryAxis: z.enum(['x', 'y']).default('x'), secondaryAxis: z.enum(['x', 'y']).optional(), bassResponse: z.number().default(40), midResponse: z.number().default(20), trebleResponse: z.number().default(5), phaseOffset: z.number().min(0).max(360).default(0), smoothingFactor: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.4), echoMode: z.boolean().optional(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [...waveformEffects] }

prompts.prompt: Develop an internal effect preset called 'gravitySlideIn' that simulates realistic gravitational physics for sliding elements into position. This effect creates animations where elements fall from above or rise from below with proper acceleration, bounce physics, and friction. Accept parameters for gravity (9.8 default, adjustable for different 'planets'), initialPosition (x,y coordinates), initialVelocity (vector), bounceDamping (0.3-0.8), friction (0-1), and maxBounces (1-5). The animation calculates parabolic trajectories for projectile motion, with proper bounce angles and energy loss. Each bounce should reduce height by bounceDamping factor, with horizontal velocity affected by friction. Include subtle rotation that correlates with horizontal velocity, creating realistic tumbling. Add optional 'dust' effects (box-shadow animations) at bounce impact points.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic with physics simulation. AnimationRange calculation: Use kinematic equations for position over time. Y-position: s = ut + 0.5at^2 for each bounce segment. X-position: linear with friction deceleration. Rotation: angular velocity proportional to horizontal speed. Generate 15-20 keyframes for smooth physics. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: calculatedPhysicsDuration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges: [translateX, translateY, rotate, boxShadow?], easingType: 'linear' }. Physics calculation: For each bounce, calculate apex, impact time, bounce velocity. Input schema: z.object({ gravity: z.number().default(9.8), initialPosition: z.object({ x: z.number(), y: z.number() }), initialVelocity: z.object({ x: z.number().default(0), y: z.number().default(0) }), bounceDamping: z.number().min(0.3).max(0.8).default(0.6), friction: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.1), maxBounces: z.number().min(1).max(5).default(3), includeDust: z.boolean().optional(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset called 'portalSlideIn' that makes elements appear to slide through dimensional portals with warping and distortion effects. This futuristic effect should create the illusion that elements are traveling through space-time, with stretching at entry, compression during travel, and expansion at exit. Accept parameters for portalShape ('circular', 'rectangular', 'irregular'), warpIntensity (distortion amount), portalColor (glow color), entryPoint (screen coordinates), exitPoint (final position), and travelDuration. The animation should include perspective transforms (perspective, rotateX, rotateY) that create 3D warping, scale transforms that stretch/compress, and filter effects for portal glow. Add animated clip-path for portal masking. Include optional 'particleStream' that creates trailing light particles using multiple box-shadows.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic with 3D transforms. AnimationRange structure: perspective with prog [0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1] and val [2000, 500, 300, 500, 1000], rotateY for spin effect, scaleX for stretch with val [1, 1.5, 0.7, 1.2, 1], scaleY inverse pattern. Filter for glow: brightness and hue-rotate animations. Clip-path: animated polygon or circle. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: travelDuration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges: [translateX, translateY, perspective, rotateX, rotateY, scaleX, scaleY, filter, clipPath], easingType: 'cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55)' }. Input schema: z.object({ portalShape: z.enum(['circular', 'rectangular', 'irregular']).default('circular'), warpIntensity: z.number().min(0).max(1).default(0.7), portalColor: z.string().default('#00ffff'), entryPoint: z.object({ x: z.number(), y: z.number() }), exitPoint: z.object({ x: z.number(), y: z.number() }), travelDuration: z.number().default(1000), particleStream: z.boolean().optional(), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [effectData] }

prompts.prompt: Design an internal effect preset called 'intelligentSlideOptimizer' that automatically analyzes target element properties and generates optimized slide-in animations. This smart effect should detect element type (text, image, video), size, position, and container context to create the most appropriate sliding animation. Accept parameters for analysisMode ('auto', 'performance', 'quality'), adaptiveSpeed (adjusts duration based on distance), smartEasing (selects easing based on element weight), collisionAvoidance (prevents overlap), and batchOptimization (groups similar elements). The effect should calculate optimal slide trajectories avoiding other elements, adjust timing based on viewport distance, and use GPU-accelerated properties. Include machine learning-inspired heuristics for choosing between translateX/Y, translate3d, or matrix transforms based on browser capabilities. Add intelligent staggering for multiple elements based on visual hierarchy.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic with adaptive generation. Analysis phase: Detect element.type, boundingBox, computedStyles, viewport position. Optimization rules: Use translate3d for GPU acceleration, matrix for complex transforms, translateX/Y for simple slides. Duration calculation: baseSpeed * (distance / viewportWidth). Easing selection: 'ease-out' for light elements, 'ease-in-out' for heavy, 'spring' for interactive. Effect data: { type: 'generic', start: calculatedDelay, duration: optimizedDuration, mode: 'provider', targetIds, ranges: [optimizedTransform, opacity?], easingType: selectedEasing, performance: { gpu: true, willChange: 'transform' } }. Input schema: z.object({ analysisMode: z.enum(['auto', 'performance', 'quality']).default('auto'), adaptiveSpeed: z.boolean().default(true), smartEasing: z.boolean().default(true), collisionAvoidance: z.boolean().default(false), batchOptimization: z.boolean().default(false), minDuration: z.number().default(300), maxDuration: z.number().default(1500), targetIds: z.array(z.string()) }). PresetMetadata: { _internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects' }. Return format: { effects: [...optimizedEffects] }
